--- a/minbpe/_rare.py
+++ b/minbpe/_rare.py
@@ -0,0 +1,212 @@
+"""
+Rarely needed code paths, imported on first use so they stay off the import
+path of the package: long-sequence merge application, the non-str training
+fallback of BasicTokenizer, and model saving / pretty printing.
+"""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+
+from .base import merge, pop_top_pairs
+
+
+def _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list over
+    the original positions plus a heap of (rank, position) entries for every
+    mergeable adjacent pair. Entries are validated lazily when popped (a pair
+    whose tokens changed is recomputed), and each round pops all entries of the
+    minimal rank in position order, i.e. sequence order. The first valid one
+    picks the pair (same as the first-seen minimal pair); its occurrences are
+    merged left to right, skipping overlaps, exactly like merge().
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]
+
+
+def _update_stats(stats, old, new, pair, idx):
+    """
+    Update pair counts (stats of old) in place so they become the stats of new,
+    where new = merge(old, pair, idx) and idx does not occur in old. Only pairs
+    touching a merged occurrence change; zero counts are removed.
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    get = stats.get
+    n_old = len(old)
+    k = new.count(idx)
+    index = new.index
+    removed = [pair]
+    rapp = removed.append
+    added = set() # pairs whose count went up
+    aadd = added.add
+    prev = -2
+    q = -1
+    for m in range(k):
+        q = index(idx, q + 1)
+        j = q + m # position of this occurrence in old
+        if q and prev != q - 1:
+            # left neighbour is untouched (an adjacent previous occurrence
+            # already accounted for the pair between them)
+            a = new[q-1]
+            p = (a, p0)
+            stats[p] -= 1
+            rapp(p)
+            p = (a, idx)
+            stats[p] = get(p, 0) + 1
+            aadd(p)
+        if j + 2 < n_old:
+            p = (p1, old[j+2])
+            stats[p] -= 1
+            rapp(p)
+            p = (idx, new[q+1])
+            stats[p] = get(p, 0) + 1
+            aadd(p)
+        prev = q
+    stats[pair] -= k
+    for p in removed:
+        if get(p) == 0:
+            del stats[p]
+    return added
+
+
+def train_ids(ids, num_merges, stats, heap, merges, vocab, verbose):
+    # BasicTokenizer training over a list of ids (token ids beyond one code point)
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    for i in range(num_merges):
+        # find the pair with the highest count; ties go to the pair whose
+        # first occurrence in ids is earliest, which is what max() over a
+        # freshly recounted dict (insertion = first-seen order) would pick
+        top, cands = pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop)
+        if len(cands) == 1:
+            pair = cands[0]
+        else:
+            cands = set(cands)
+            for p in zip(ids, ids[1:]):
+                if p in cands:
+                    pair = p
+                    break
+        # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+        idx = 256 + i
+        # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
+        new = merge(ids, pair, idx)
+        for p in _update_stats(stats, ids, new, pair, idx):
+            heappush(heap, (-stats[p], p))
+        ids = new
+        # save the merge
+        merges[pair] = idx
+        vocab[idx] = vocab[pair[0]] + vocab[pair[1]]
+        # prints
+        if verbose:
+            print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")
+
+
+def replace_control_characters(s: str) -> str:
+    # we don't want to print control characters
+    # which distort the output (e.g. \n or much worse)
+    # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4324790/removing-control-characters-from-a-string-in-python/19016117#19016117
+    # http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr44/#GC_Values_Table
+    import unicodedata
+    chars = []
+    for ch in s:
+        if unicodedata.category(ch)[0] != "C":
+            chars.append(ch) # this character is ok
+        else:
+            chars.append(f"\\u{ord(ch):04x}") # escape
+    return "".join(chars)
+
+
+def render_token(t: bytes) -> str:
+    # pretty print a token, escaping control characters
+    s = t.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
+    s = replace_control_characters(s)
+    return s
+
+
+def save(tok, file_prefix):
+    # see Tokenizer.save
+    # write the model: to be used in load() later
+    model_file = file_prefix + ".model"
+    with open(model_file, 'w') as f:
+        # write the version, pattern and merges, that's all that's needed
+        f.write("minbpe v1\n")
+        f.write(f"{tok.pattern}\n")
+        # write the special tokens, first the number of them, then each one
+        f.write(f"{len(tok.special_tokens)}\n")
+        for special, idx in tok.special_tokens.items():
+            f.write(f"{special} {idx}\n")
+        # the merges dict
+        for idx1, idx2 in tok.merges:
+            f.write(f"{idx1} {idx2}\n")
+    # write the vocab: for the human to look at
+    vocab_file = file_prefix + ".vocab"
+    inverted_merges = {idx: pair for pair, idx in tok.merges.items()}
+    with open(vocab_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        for idx, token in tok.vocab.items():
+            # note: many tokens may be partial utf-8 sequences
+            # and cannot be decoded into valid strings. Here we're using
+            # errors='replace' to replace them with the replacement char �.
+            # this also means that we couldn't possibly use .vocab in load()
+            # because decoding in this way is a lossy operation!
+            s = render_token(token)
+            # find the children of this token, if any
+            if idx in inverted_merges:
+                # if this token has children, render it nicely as a merge
+                idx0, idx1 = inverted_merges[idx]
+                s0 = render_token(tok.vocab[idx0])
+                s1 = render_token(tok.vocab[idx1])
+                f.write(f"[{s0}][{s1}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
+            else:
+                # otherwise this is leaf token, just print it
+                # (this should just be the first 256 tokens, the bytes)
+                f.write(f"[{s}] {idx}\n")
+
